detailed_description:
The target is a clean full-screen hand-drawn 2D cartoon, with soft painted spring park scenery in the style of <Subject 3>. A pale beige path lies before green trees, small flowers and distant blue-green hills. Warm morning sunlight comes from the upper right.
[Shot 1] A fixed medium two-shot frames the two characters from the knees upward with both complete heads, ears and hands visible. Bobo <Subject 2> is on the left, and 99 <Subject 1> is on the right, each turned three-quarters toward the other. They stand at an easy conversational distance on the park path. The composition remains stable throughout five seconds. From 0.2 to 2.1 seconds the rabbit <Subject 1>, with a bright medium-high youthful female Mandarin voice, a light warm timbre and clear standard pronunciation (S1), looks at the bear, smiles and says: <d>[Chinese] 今天精神真好！</d> The bear listens with his lips closed and eyes directed toward her. After a small pause, from 2.4 to 4.5 seconds the bear <Subject 2>, with a warm medium-low youthful male Mandarin voice, rounded timbre and clear standard pronunciation (S2), answers her with a relaxed smile: <d>[Chinese] 因为有你陪我呀！</d> The rabbit listens during his turn and gives one small happy nod near the end. The two visible mouths articulate their respective lines. The final half second holds the pair smiling at each other with their hands relaxed at their sides.

overall_soundscape:
Quiet morning birds and a light breeze through the leaves remain below the two foreground Mandarin speaking turns. The short pause between the lines stays clear.

A 15-second live-action reinterpretation of the Cowboy Bebop anime opening: adult space-noir bounty hunters, propulsive jazz, graphic cobalt-blue, mustard-yellow and vermilion accents, cool confidence and sudden bursts of physical action. A complete miniature opening sequence with a beginning, energetic middle and memorable ending. 16:9 widescreen, 24 fps.

REFERENCE ROLES
Picture 1 is the live-action casting and costume reference for Spike Spiegel: the same slim adult man with tousled dark hair, blue suit, yellow shirt and narrow black tie throughout. Picture 2 is the live-action casting and costume reference for Faye Valentine: the same adult woman with a short dark violet bob, yellow outfit, red jacket and cream boots throughout. Preserve their distinct faces, hair, clothes and adult proportions. Use these as character references, not as fixed compositions or starting frames. The two people are different characters; never merge their identities or clothing. Only these two principal characters are needed. Do not display the reference photographs or character sheets.

VISUAL TREATMENT
Convincing live-action cinema with real human skin, fabric, hair, practical sets, physically believable running and natural expressions. Subtle 35mm film grain, crisp faces, rich black shadows, cool blue night light and warm amber highlights, wet pavement, lightly drifting steam. Retro-futuristic spaceport streets and weathered spacecraft interiors, with tactile photographed miniature spacecraft for the exterior. Fast confident editing and varied shot sizes. Most of the frame remains photographic. At two edit points only, a flat yellow or red horizontal bar briefly crosses the lower third and clears on the beat; it never covers a face. No subtitles, credits, logos or other displayed text.

SHOT 1, 0.0-2.5 seconds — THE CITY WAKES
Wide street-level shot in a blue-hour spaceport alley. Spike from Picture 1 is already visible near the foreground. He walks three relaxed steps toward the camera through a shaft of amber light, lifts his chin and notices something off to his right. His jacket and loose tie sway. The camera tracks backward gently; distant elevated traffic and steam give the city life. Hard cut on a brass accent.

SHOT 2, 2.5-5.0 seconds — THE CHASE
Medium-wide side tracking shot. The same Spike accelerates into a real run across the wet alley, with clearly alternating footfalls and natural arm swings. He leaps over one low puddle, lands and keeps running. The camera follows him laterally; background lights streak slightly while his face and suit remain coherent. A narrow mustard-yellow graphic bar sweeps across the bottom edge for an instant at the edit, then clears. Hard cut, no morph.

SHOT 3, 5.0-7.5 seconds — FAYE
Medium shot inside a spacecraft passage. Faye from Picture 2 pushes open a heavy teal metal door, takes a confident step through it and turns her gaze toward the camera with a small knowing smile. She pulls the red jacket back onto one shoulder as she continues moving. The camera makes a short lateral move. Warm doorway light defines her real face and violet bob. Hard cut on the snare.

SHOT 4, 7.5-10.0 seconds — SPIKE'S RHYTHM
Low medium-wide shot with the same Spike on a rain-darkened landing platform. He plants a foot, turns his body in a quick controlled pivot and performs one fluid high side kick into empty space, then lands in a balanced stance and relaxes his shoulders. His blue jacket flares then settles. One action, clear start and finish, realistic joints and contact with the ground. A vermilion lower-third bar sweeps briefly across the bottom at the edit and clears. No opponent, no injury, no gunfire. Hard cut.

SHOT 5, 10.0-12.5 seconds — INTO ORBIT
Exterior wide shot, photographed miniature realism. Spike's small red retro-futuristic single-seat space fighter, with very long thin straight wings and a central glass cockpit, flies across frame above a curving blue planet. Its engine glows orange; the craft banks smoothly to reveal its underside and recedes toward a field of stars. A slow pan follows its flight. Keep this a space exterior without people floating in space. Hard cut.

SHOT 6, 12.5-15.0 seconds — SPACE COWBOYS
Medium two-shot in a dim spacecraft observation passage, planet and stars visible through a broad window. Spike from Picture 1 stands on the left and Faye from Picture 2 stands on the right. Spike settles against the window frame, loosens his shoulders and gives a faint crooked smile; Faye takes a final half-step beside him, folds her arms and glances toward him. The camera pushes in slightly as their hair and clothing settle. Finish on their calm, recognizable faces against the blue planet. Only the final 0.4 seconds become still. No end card and no fade to black.

AUDIO
A continuous, clearly audible original instrumental big-band jazz-funk cue: agile baritone saxophone riff, punchy brass stabs, walking upright bass and tight live drum kit, brisk swing feel around 150 BPM. Start the music immediately, build its energy through the chase and kick, and finish with one confident brass-and-drum accent in the last half-second. Compose a new musical phrase; do not reproduce the melody or recording of Tank!. No vocals, spoken countdown, dialogue or narration. Under the music, quiet shoe impacts on wet ground, one metal door clunk, fabric movement and a brief low spacecraft engine whoosh at the exterior cut. Music remains the dominant layer.

AVOID
Anime rendering, cartoon outlines, painted people, plastic CG faces, doll skin, cosplay event footage, frozen poster montage, motion confined to transitions, duplicated characters, identity swaps, clothing changes, malformed hands or legs, floating feet, impossible joints, crossfades or face morphs, persistent split screens, excessive slow motion, random camera shaking, text, watermarks, subtitles, speech or singing.

method.visual_scope: All listed contacts and native final frames were actually viewed. Long frames 144-176 and running frames 0-12 were inspected contiguously. This is sampled image review, not every-frame continuous audiovisual playback.
